case_title: State of Gujarat & Anr. v. Narayan @ Narayan Sai @ Mota Bhagwan Asaram @ Asumal Harpalani
accused_socioeconomic_status: Alleged by the DGP's order: has a financial background and a network of persons; properties worth crores of rupees seized in investigation (alleged, not found by the Court)
previous_criminal_record: Yes - seven other offences registered against the accused (as stated in the DGP's order); no prior conviction is stated
aggravating_circumstances: Gravity of the sexual and other offences; alleged threats, assaults and murders of witnesses by followers; attempts to bribe public officials; threats to police officials; mass following; illegal mobile phone and outside contacts in jail
mitigating_circumstances: Argued by the respondent: no violation during December 2020 furlough; no complaints since 2016; ill health of father and mother. The Supreme Court did not accept these as sufficient
trial_court_outcome: Convicted; life imprisonment with fine of Rs. 1,00,000 under s.376(2) and s.377; shorter concurrent terms for other sections; compensation of Rs. 5,00,000 under s.357(3) CrPC
high_court_outcome: Petition under s.482 CrPC allowed; DGP's order of 8 May 2021 set aside; furlough of 14 days granted
offence_finally_established: Not decided in this appeal; conviction under appeal before the High Court, so no offence finally established here
neutral_facts: An FIR was registered on 6 October 2013 at a police station against the accused for sexual offences against a female complainant under the Indian Penal Code, along with intimidation, hurt and conspiracy offences. The judgment does not describe the particulars of the sexual offence itself. During the investigation, a senior police officer who guided the arrest team had her official phone number disclosed to the media. She then received calls from a person claiming to be a follower of the accused, threatening to kill her if she continued the search. A follower of the accused was alleged to have offered a bribe of Rs. 1 crore, and bribes were allegedly offered to police, medical and judicial officers to weaken the case. The complainant's husband, a witness in the trial, was allegedly assaulted with a lethal weapon in February 2014. Further assaults on other witnesses were alleged in March and May 2014, one of which allegedly resulted in death during treatment. Authorities attributed these attacks to followers of the accused and alleged that a visitor to the accused in jail in February 2014 was linked to the offences. Authorities also alleged that a large quantity of cash and property connected to the accused's network was seized. These matters are as alleged by the authorities in their objections to furlough.
physical_harm: Not stated for the victim. Per the authorities' allegations, witnesses were assaulted in 2014 and 2015 incidents; one witness allegedly died during treatment
number_of_offences: 13 charged; finally upheld: Not stated (Supreme Court did not decide conviction)
financial_property_loss: Not applicable to the victim. Alleged bribe of Rs. 1 crore offered; compensation of Rs. 5,00,000 ordered by the trial court
motive: Not identified (the court did not decide motive; the only motive mentioned is alleged: to break the morale of the complainant, for the witness assaults)
key_evidence_accepted: The DGP's order of 8 May 2021 and the opinions of the ACP, DCP and Jail Superintendent, which the Court held not perverse. No trial evidence was assessed
witness_credibility: Not assessed. The Court accepted the authorities' opinions as not perverse
post_offence_conduct: Court noted jail conduct not shown to be above reproach (illegal mobile phone, attempted outside contacts). After the December 2020 furlough and interim bail, the respondent surrendered to authorities; no escape found
custody_duration: About seven and a half years of imprisonment, as recorded in the High Court's finding
bail_history: Temporary bail: 3 weeks from 16 April 2015; 2 days from 15 February 2019; furlough from 5 December 2020 (14 days); temporary bail 31 January to 3 February 2021
trial_duration: offence: not given (FIR registered 6 October 2013); trial judgment: 30 April 2019; High Court: 24 June 2021; Supreme Court: 20 October 2021
legal_representation: Accused (respondent): Sanjiv Punalekar, Suvidutt M. S., Ankush Mahajan, Dharma Raj, Mrs. Anu B., Ms. Vijayalakshmi Raju, Mrs. Dhanya C., Advocates. State: Tushar Mehta, Solicitor General, with Kanu Agrawal and Aniruddha P. Mayee, Advocates
investigation_status: FIR registered 6 October 2013; charges framed; trial completed with judgment on 30 April 2019
procedural_irregularity: Court noted the High Court's December 2020 furlough order did not deal with the authorities' objections. No other procedural lapse noted
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted on 30 April 2019. High Court (Single Judge): respondent's petition allowed on 24 June 2021, furlough granted. Supreme Court: State's appeal allowed; High Court order set aside
prosecution_argument: Furlough is discretionary and subject to Rule 4 (public peace, conduct, escape); the DGP's objections are not perverse; the High Court's reliance on its earlier order is misplaced; the gross nature of the crimes, witness threats and bribery disentitle relief
defence_argument: Furlough is a matter of right; father is critically ill with no family around him; no untoward incident during four earlier releases; the allegations are unproven; the Rule 3(2) proviso allows furlough every year
legal_principle_applied: Rules 3, 4 and 17 confer no legal right to furlough; furlough is discretionary and balanced against public interest; the sanctioning authority's opinion is reviewed only for perversity or extraneous considerations
precedent_relied_upon: State of Maharashtra v. Suresh Pandurang Darvakar (2006) 4 SCC 776; Asfaq v. State of Rajasthan (2017) 15 SCC 55; State of Haryana v. Mohinder Singh (2000) 3 SCC 394
judicial_aggravating_factors: Threat to the complainant and deposing witnesses; attempts to threaten and suborn investigators and witnesses; mass following; attempts to bribe public officials; conduct in jail not above reproach
other_sentence_order: High Court's order of 24 June 2021 set aside; furlough refused; pending applications disposed of
